subject: Vendor cascade notice — EdgeWave subcontracting request & DPA checklist
content:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgewave.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor cascade notice — EdgeWave subcontracting request & DPA checklist

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, EdgeWave plans to subcontract a portion of the log-ingest pipeline to a regional partner (Logix) that will perform transient parsing and enrichment for US customers. Before we can proceed we need: a) a short description of the subprocessor's role/scope, b) confirmation of the data types processed (PII? tokens? raw logs?), and c) the DPA annex and evidence we require for flow‑down (SOC 2, KMS handling, and retention controls).

Attached: EdgeWave_OrderForm_redlines_v1.docx (order form with proposed clause to capture subcontracting authorization and DPA annex references) and DPA_evidence_manifest.csv (requested artifact list).

High-level asks from Redwood:
- Explicit scope for Logix limited to parsing/enrichment (no model hosting or training).
- Data residency: US-only processing for accounts contracted with US residency.
- KV cache/access: Logix must not retain any raw customer data beyond 72 hours and must support log deletion on request.
- Security artifacts: current SOC 2 Type II report, encryption-at-rest key custody details (HSM or customer KMS?), and network segregation diagram.

Can you confirm if Logix accepts flow-down of the DPA (annex A) and whether they will sign our standard subprocessor rider? If not, flag the clauses they cannot accept so we can scope legal redlines.

Proposed timeline: we need initial confirmation + artifacts by EOD Tue (24 Jun) to make the July rollout date. If there are objections, we’ll need to loop Legal and Procurement for a decision.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0143

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgewave.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor cascade notice — EdgeWave subcontracting request & DPA checklist

Sean / Alex —

Thanks for the packet, Alex. I reviewed the redlined order form and pulled out the legal items I expect to be friction points so we can triage: 

1) Clause 5.2 (Subprocessor authorization): EdgeWave added a blanket right to subcontract which we prefer to keep scoped by named subprocessors + notification + opt‑out for regulated customers. Request: change to named/approved subprocessors or, if necessary, a 30‑day customer notification window.

2) DPA annex reference: the redline points to EdgeWave's DPA rather than Redwood's annex. We need EdgeWave to either accept Redwood's DPA flows or allow a mutual annex where Logix agrees to Redwood's processing terms.

3) Deletion / Retention: redline currently says Logix retains "as needed" — need concrete retention window (72 hours) and proof of deletion on request.

4) Incident reporting / breach notification: specify 72‑hour notification to Redwood and support for customer notifications.

If Logix pushes back on signing Redwood's annex, Legal is likely to accept a signed subprocessor rider with materially equivalent language plus the SOC 2 + encryption evidence and an attestation from an officer.

I’ll draft a short rider template we can send if Alex confirms Logix is the only option. Lauren — can you prepare the DPA annex template and highlight the non‑negotiables (retention, residency, breach notification, KMS custody)?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

---

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgewave.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, procurement@procureco.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor cascade notice — EdgeWave subcontracting request & DPA checklist

Sean / Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear ask list. Quick responses inline: 

- Scope: Logix will handle JSON parsing, schema normalization, and enrichment tags only. They will not host models or retain raw logs beyond the enrichment step.
- Data types: primarily service logs, occasional user identifiers (hashed IDs), and non-sensitive metadata. No full transcripts or content blobs for now.
- Residency: Logix operates US‑only datacenters (East/West) and will restrict processing to US customers by configuration.
- Retention: Logix agrees to the 72‑hour retention window for temporary artifacts.
- Evidence: attached SOC2_type2_certificate.pdf and a short KMS notice. Procurement is copying in their procurement contact to coordinate the signed rider.

EdgeWave requests two minor edits to Redwood's rider: (1) an ability for EdgeWave to notify and onboard replacement subprocessors in a 10‑day window (vs 30), and (2) carveout language for aggregated telemetry used for product operations (not customer content). If those are deal‑breakers, let us know and we can escalate.

We are aiming to have the signed subprocessor rider and artifacts to you by EOD Thu (26 Jun).

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Partnerships | EdgeWave
alex.chen@edgewave.io | +1 (415) 555‑0220

Attachment stubs: SOC2_type2_certificate.pdf (11 pages), KMS_notice.txt (1 page)

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor cascade notice — EdgeWave subcontracting request & DPA checklist

Team —

Good progress. Summary / next steps: 
- EdgeWave confirmed scope + 72‑hour retention and provided SOC2 artifact — Kimberly, please validate SOC2 scope covers Logix functions.
- EdgeWave asked for a 10‑day replacement notice and telemetry carveout. Legal: prioritise whether 10 days + telemetry aggregated metrics is acceptable; if so we can proceed with rider signing.
- Lauren: please pull together Redwood's DPA annex with the highlighted non‑negotiables (retention, residency, breach notification, KMS custody) and a short subprocessor rider template. Attach to Drive link and we’ll send to Alex for countersign.

If Legal gives greenlight on the two minor asks, we route DocuSign (link above) and Procurement will close the order form amendment. If Legal rejects, escalate to Head of Revenue and Head of Legal for decision.

I’ll queue a 30‑minute sync tomorrow AM if we need to triage live.

Thanks —
Sean
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
